description: Random voltages joined by six different transition shapes, in 4HP, so the outputs move rather than jump

params.text: Sets how often a new random value is picked, from 0.0039Hz fully counter-clockwise to 1024Hz fully clockwise
Sets how wide a span the random values are drawn from, 0V for one fixed voltage to 10V at the far right
Sets where the span falls: its centre, or its bottom or top, according to the button beside it, -10V to +10V
Weights the odds within the span: counter-clockwise favours the middle or the minimum, clockwise favours the edges or the maximum, according to the mode button below it
Attenuates and inverts the rate CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Attenuates and inverts the range CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Attenuates and inverts the anchor CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Attenuates and inverts the distribution CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Steps the anchor knob's meaning through minimum, centre and maximum, with a light showing which
Switches what the two ends of the distribution knob favour: the centre and the edges, or the minimum and the maximum
Holds a change of span until the next random value is picked, so a curve already under way is left alone
Makes each new value land in the opposite half of the span from the one before, which turns the output into alternating rises and falls; it is ignored in Min/Max distribution

inputs.text: Moves the rate, every volt here doubling it after the trim knob
Adds its voltage to the span after the trim knob, which can carry the span past the knob's own 10V
Adds its voltage to the anchor after the trim knob
Moves the distribution, 5V covering half the knob's travel at full trim

outputs.text: Fires a 1ms pulse each time a new random value is picked, which marks the start of every curve segment
Carries a straight line from the last value to the next
Carries the last value held, then a jump to the next halfway through, like a sample and hold
Carries an S-shaped curve from the last value to the next, easing out of one and into the other
Carries the S-curve turned inside out, so it leaves one value fast and arrives at the next fast, with a sharp corner at each
Carries whichever of the four shapes the menu sets for it, logarithmic unless you change it; a mark beside it shows the shape in colour

notes: every output moves between the same random values at the same moments; only the shape of the journey differs
this module is monophonic; the curves come out on one channel each
menu: User 1 curve mode, User 2 curve mode: Log, Exp, Top rounded/bottom sharp, Bottom rounded/top sharp — sets the shape that output uses, shown by its mark in green, red, blue or orange
Set min/max-range — sets the range and anchor knobs together to a named pair of voltages
Distibution-range: 60% (value-range not affected) up to 100% — narrows what the distribution knob covers, so a full turn no longer collapses the span to one voltage
LFO rate chaos — picks a new random speed for each cycle, so the curve segments run at uneven lengths
Quantize mode — rounds the output to the nearest step of the size chosen, from a twelfth of a volt up to 5V, and is Off unless you set it
Clipping range — clamps every output to the range chosen, -12V to 12V unless you change it, and Off lets the output run to any voltage
Process quality: Audio, High, Balanced, Low, Very low — sets how often the module runs its algorithm, from every cycle down to every 256th; below Balanced a 1ms trigger can be missed
Auto select process quality — picks the process quality from the dialled-in rate and from which ports are patched, and greys out the manual choice while it is on
Trigger-high output-level — sets the voltage a trigger pulse carries during its 1ms high phase, 10V unless you change it
Trigger-low output-level — sets the voltage a trigger output carries between pulses, 0V unless you change it
